facts.big: passado simples + present perfect + said/told that
facts.label: Relatar um fato
facts.sub: Use o passado simples para o tempo, o present perfect para o resultado agora e said/told me that + passado para contar o que alguém disse: I’ve lost my wallet.

facts.label: Resultado agora
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para um fato com resultado no presente: I’ve lost my wallet. Com ever, never, yet e already: Have you called the police yet? Sem tempo passado exato.

facts.label: Quando foi
facts.sub: Use o passado simples quando o tempo é passado e fechado: I paid for a coffee at ten. Palavras comuns: yesterday, at ten, last night. Compare: I’ve lost it e I lost it at ten.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Present perfect shows a result now.
We say “I have lost it yesterday”.
items.why: We say I lost it yesterday.

items.s: In reported speech, said that + past simple is common.
items.why: He said that he saw it.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Present perfect shows a result now. → Verdadeiro (I’ve lost my wallet.)
We say “I have lost it yesterday”. → Falso (We say I lost it yesterday.)
In reported speech, said that + past simple is common. → Verdadeiro (He said that he saw it.)

pages.title: A busy street · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a busy Friday morning on a street in London. Red buses pass slowly, and people hurry to work. Ivan stops at the corner with a worried face. His wallet is not in his pocket anymore. Ana is walking to the station when he asks for help. She stops and listens to his story.
“Excuse me, Ana. I’ve lost my wallet. Have you seen it?” says Ivan. “No, I haven’t. When did you last have it?” says Ana. “I paid for a coffee at ten, and then I walked here.” says Ivan.

pages.title: A busy street · 3/3
paragraphs: “Look! A woman is waving. She said that she found a wallet.” says Ana. “That’s it! Thank you so much. You’ve been really kind to me.” says Ivan. Ivan opens the wallet and checks his cards and money. Everything is still inside, even the photo of his family. The woman smiles and says it was lying on the pavement. Ivan offers her a reward, but she says no. Ana looks at her watch and runs to the station. Good people are everywhere, even in a big city.
